handoff_contract_choices: alert_policy.evaluate(game_event, matches) returns Alert items in the store.put_alert shape (providerRoute added by the pipeline), at most one per (profileId, eventId), only for profiles in matches; it reads Settings via store.get_profile and earlier alerts via store.list_alerts. Matches are the P2-B04T shape {profileId, eventId, revision, starters, cursor}; inputs are fixtures, the stub matcher is never called.

GameEvent gap: the Phase 2 data model (store.put_event, normalize_summary) has no quarter or scoring flag, yet close game needs Q4/OT and player score needs a scoring play. Tests pass two ESPN play fields on the event: period (int; 4 = Q4, >=5 = OT) and scoringPlay (bool). P2-B05's write set (backend/src/alert_policy/) cannot add them to feed_ingest/store; see remaining risks.

Settings follow the landed TV ProfileCodec wire shape: alertTypes in {RedZone, PlayerScore, CloseGame}; frequency = alert_min_gap seconds; quietHours [{startMinute, endMinute}] (may wrap midnight); gameDayPeriods {enabled, periods}; spoilerDelay seconds; excitement Off|Mild|Hype; detectionOptIn bool. Minutes of day are read in UTC from eventTime (Settings carry no time zone). Window end-minute boundaries are avoided; start minutes are inclusive. gameDayPeriods.enabled false is not relied on.

Red zone: fieldPosition (ESPN yardsToEndzone) strictly below 20 and possession equal to a matched starter's team. Player score: scoringPlay with a matched starter in playerIds. Close game: period >= 4 and |home - away| <= 8, once per game while the state lasts (re-entry not tested).
Simultaneous types: one alert; alertType is one of the matching enabled types; triggerContext.alertTypes lists every matching enabled type.

triggerContext carries gameId, eventId, source, score, starters (with athlete_id), alertTypes and basis (observed-playback | profile-assumption); opted-out profiles are always profile-assumption. Whether an opted-out profile still receives alerts is not decided here.

emittedAt is the release time (>= eventTime + spoilerDelay); alert_min_gap compares release times of released alerts of the same game; suppressed events never consume the gap (the observable form of the gate order).

commentary: None/absent at Off; fixed template strings at Mild/Hype, different from each other, identical for identical inputs; every digit run is a score, the margin, the field position, the period or 20; no lineup name or team outside the trigger. Red-zone text must not match the on-field/will-score pattern in policy_support.OVERCLAIM.
A match with a cursor revises that alert: the returned alert keeps the cursor and carries the new revision.

alert_policy.pending(profile_id, cursor) returns {alerts, cursor: str}: only this profile's alerts after cursor with emittedAt not in the future, in cursor order; the cursor never passes a held alert. Envelope: schemaVersion 1, id = cursor, revision, source = triggerContext.source, updatedAt = emittedAt, data {alertType, triggerContext, commentary, route = stored providerRoute}.
Alert type vocabulary follows the TV enum (RedZone/PlayerScore/CloseGame); P2-B04T's seed rows use 'playerScore' only as an opaque stored value.
